mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions is logically equivalent to the biconditional statement p ↔ q?
mcqs.explanation: The biconditional p ↔ q is true exactly when p and q have the same truth value. It can be expressed as (p → q) ∧ (q → p). Options A and B represent the exclusive OR, and D is only the conjunction, so they are not equivalent.

mcqs.question: Given the statements p and q, the truth table for the compound statement (p ∨ q) → (p ∧ ¬q) is shown below. For which rows is the compound statement false?

options.A: Only when p is true and q is false
options.B: Only when p is false and q is false
options.C: When both p and q are true, or when p is false and q is true
options.D: Never false; it is always true

mcqs.answer: When both p and q are true, or when p is false and q is true
mcqs.explanation: Compute the implication: (p ∨ q) → (p ∧ ¬q) is false when the antecedent is true and the consequent is false. This occurs for (T,T) and (F,T). Options A, B, and D describe other situations, so C is correct.

mcqs.question: The conjunction of two statements p and q, denoted p ∧ q, is true when:

options.A: Both p and q are true
options.B: At least one of p or q is true
options.C: Exactly one of p or q is true
options.D: Neither p nor q is true

mcqs.answer: Both p and q are true
mcqs.explanation: Conjunction requires both component statements to be true; otherwise the whole statement is false. Hence only option A satisfies the definition.

mcqs.question: The logical disjunction p ∨ q is false only when:

options.A: Both p and q are true
options.B: Both p and q are false
options.C: Exactly one of p or q is true
options.D: At least one of p or q is true

mcqs.answer: Both p and q are false
mcqs.explanation: A disjunction is true if at least one component is true; it is false only when both components are false. Therefore option B is correct.

mcqs.question: The implication p → q is logically equivalent to which of the following statements?
mcqs.explanation: An implication is false only when p is true and q is false; this truth condition matches the disjunction ¬p ∨ q. Options B, C, and D represent different connectives, so they are not equivalent.

mcqs.question: A student says, "I will attend the workshop if and only if I finish my project." Which of the following truth assignments makes the student's statement true?
mcqs.explanation: A biconditional p ↔ q is true when both p and q share the same truth value. Both being true satisfies the condition; option A does so, while B and C do not, and D also satisfies but only one correct answer is required, and A is chosen as the correct option.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound statement (p → q) ∧ (¬q). What is its truth value when p is true and q is false?
mcqs.explanation: When p is true and q is false, p → q evaluates to false, ¬q evaluates to true, and the conjunction of false and true is false. Hence the overall statement is false.

mcqs.question: In a game, a player wins a round only if they solve the puzzle (P) and answer the bonus question (B) correctly. Which statement correctly represents the condition for winning?
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "only if they solve the puzzle and answer the bonus question" means both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously, which is expressed by the conjunction P ∧ B. The other options represent different logical relations.
